title: TX annual Jan-open to Jul-1 rally, Fibonacci pullback re-entry
question: For each year TX rallies from January's open to July 1st, do the 0.618/0.5/0.382 Fibonacci retracement levels of that rally (entered independently when touched, exited the following March 31) show a meaningful win rate, given only ~13 candidate years exist in the available daily history?
hypothesis: This is an exploratory, low-sample-size seasonal-pattern test, not a validated edge; the small n (7-8 trades per level) means results should be read as descriptive, not decision-grade, until a materially longer or higher-frequency dataset is available.

findings.title: Sample size is inherently tiny (7-8 trades per level)
findings.detail: Only 13 candidate years exist in the available daily history (2013-2025); every level's 95% confidence interval spans roughly 30-50 percentage points. Read every win rate below as descriptive, not as a validated edge.

findings.title: The 0.5 level shows the highest win rate in this small sample
findings.detail: n=8, 62.5% win rate, PF 3.557 -- but n=8 with a 95% CI of 30.57-86.32% means this is consistent with anywhere from a coin-flip to a strong edge.

findings.title: 0.382 (the shallowest, most-often-touched level) has the weakest win rate
findings.detail: n=8, 50.0% win rate -- shallower retracements trigger more often but, in this sample, land closer to a coin flip than the deeper levels.

card_summary: The January-to-July TX rally and where its pullbacks land on a Fibonacci grid.
